title: Orchestrated state replay with economic thresholds and batch cache safeguards
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Problem: config rollouts that touch batching and KV cache parameters can produce subtle cost regressions or correctness regressions that only appear under production traffic patterns. We need an automated rollback orchestration that is safe (no noisy flip-flopping), cost-aware (prefers inexpensive mitigations), and state-consistent (reconciles KV cache + batch state before/after rollbacks). Goal: implement a staged apply+monitor+replay system that can perform deterministic dry-run replay of recent requests, detect economic and correctness anomalies, and trigger a controlled rollback or rollforward depending on confidence and cost heuristics. Must integrate with Console alerts and the existing change application pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Can run a shadow apply simulation for 10k recent requests against candidate config without impacting live traffic
Detects degradation signals (latency p99 + token cost per request + divergence rate) and raises a rollback suggestion within 5 minutes of threshold breach
Rollback decision respects an economic hysteresis band: does not auto-revert for transient <5% cost blips; escalates for sustained >10% regressions over 10 minutes
KV cache is reconciled post-rollback: prefixes added by the candidate config are either flushed or mapped back so serving does not observe stale mixed state
Includes a 'safe replay' runbook accessible from Console with one-click start and link to GitHub PR that performed the config change
Has automated tests covering dry-run result comparison and simulated rollback state transition in CI
design_notes: Prefer shadow-apply (no production traffic) for initial validation; shadow runs reuse production trace but mark outputs as simulated
Introduce economic hysteresis band to avoid noisy auto-reverts: combine short-window signal and longer-window confirmation
Use probabilistic anomaly scorer (ensemble of latency, error-rate, token-cost delta) rather than single metric thresholds
KV cache reconciliation model: capture prefix diffs at apply time and create an idempotent rollback script that either remaps prefixes or performs targeted invalidation
Trade-offs: full transactional apply would be ideal but is high complexity across heterogeneous runtimes; we opt for staged shadow + partial transactional guardpoints
implementation_plan: Step 1: Add trace replay harness that can feed a sampled set of recent requests into a staging runtime with candidate config (2d)
Step 2: Implement anomaly scoring library and telemetry hooks (3d)
Step 3: Build economic hysteresis controller with configurable short/long windows and thresholds (2d)
Step 4: KV prefix capture & rollback script generator (3d)
Step 5: Console integration: one-click runbook, links to PRs and telemetry, and manual rollback button (2d)
Step 6: E2E tests in CI including simulated production traces and deterministic state reconciliation checks (2d)
Step 7: Canary rollouts with progressive traffic and automatic rollback gating (2d)
Estimated total: 14 development days spread across two engineers with staggered overlaps
rollback_triggers: error-rate or 5xx spike above configured SLA breach
KV cache consistency errors reported by runtime inspector
testing_plan: Unit tests for anomaly scorer with synthetic signal injection
Integration test: replay 10k traces into staging runtime with golden baseline comparator
Chaos test: simulate partial rollout and network partitions while exercising rollback scripts
Telemetry test: assert alerts and Console links populate within expected latency
Dry-run test: ensure rollback scripts are idempotent and safe to rerun
